questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was important that the culture was different from my home culture, and that the language spoken in the given country was a language I hadn't previously been exposed to.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
It was very difficult to find the information I needed in terms of acceptance to the host university as well as what to expect next. The incoming mobility coordinator at Eötvös Loránd University was rude and didn't seem as if she wanted to help the incoming students, however, they had a new coordinator appointed some time during the semester who does her job well. 
All in all, it was not easy to figure out how to access information. Moreover, we received two emails on orientation, but the second email a lot of us did not receive, which of course caused a lot of stir and stress among us, because we had missed important information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: None. We were told we would have a tutor, but the tutor never contacted me, and when I contacted her, she said she was on vacation, but that she would contact me when she returned, but she never did.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The orientation barely existed, this can and should be done much better.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very easy to find off-campus housing, I simply used Facebook. I didn't find anything until I arrived in Budapest, as I wanted to be able to go and see the place before I said yes to anything, to be certain that it was not a scam. Also I awaited an answer on whether or not I had been appointed campus housing. It is very easy to find accommodation, as Budapest is a big city with many students.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I don't really know? I didn't know any exchange students who lived on campus, as I expect these actually are offered to the students of Eötvös Loránd University.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The on-campus housing is not satisfactory, as I actually applied almost 1 year before I went, but I was still declined. I don't think any Erasmus students received one.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
This was an absolute nightmare. We were supposed to contact all the professors and ask if we could attend their courses and get their signature, and because of COVID everything was done online which made it more difficult. 

Moreover, the course catalogue for MA students was not very good, something that the students of Eötvös Loránd University filed a complaint about as well.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
We would be notified of the process 1 week before we had to register. 
We were to contact the professors of the courses we wanted to attend. 
When the professor gave us permission to attend the course, we needed a signature. 
When all your courses had been accepted by the professors, we needed to send the signatures to the incoming mobility. 
However, because everything was online, we could also just send the emails from the professors to the coordinator.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not much help, as the previous coordinator was still the only help, and she didn't help us very much. Often times she didn't reply at all, so we were kind of left alone.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I registered for all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be prepared that it is an absolute mess, but the coordinator is much nicer now, so she will definetly be more helpful.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
The course catalogue wasn't very interesting, and some of the professors are not very engaged or relies too much on peer teaching and cancels class from time to time. 
However, I had some great courses with very enthusiastic professors who were really motivating and good at teaching, making it a great experience. I learned a lot during this stay, because of the enthusiasm, things that I initially didn't expect to find interesting.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of courses was good and fairly high in some courses, however, when term paper/exams came it was obvious that they haven't been taught how to write an academic paper, so the level of academic papers weren't too high compared to UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching was very different, as you receive a mark for your participation as well, meaning that a lot more participated in the class discussions and that made it even more interesting.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Gender in Modern and Contemporary fiction 
Modernist Women 
The History of Political Humour
English Varieties 
Problems in Germanic Phonology 
21st Century Critical Theory 
Corpus Linguistics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I recommend The History of Political History, generally any course with the professor in this course. Moreover, 21st Century Critical Theory, Gender in Contemporary Fiction, and if interested in phonology and the like choose English Varieities.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Transportation was less expensive, housing was more expensive than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not attend any.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were a lot of sports courses, but I did not attend.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to Open Mics or attend a gym with classes, that is how I learned the most about Hungarian culture. When you get there you basically live in an erasmus bobble, but by going somewhere where the majority is Hungarian, you learn something completely different.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to Margeret Island, go to Eger, Esztergom, etc.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy! People are very welcoming in Hungary, some might be quite annoyed that you speak English, but that may just be because they are not able to. Learn some phrases and words in Hungarian, and you're good to go.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just talk to them, they are very interested in you and why you chose Hungary.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not that many differences actually, rather the language.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I appreciate their welcoming spirit and their curiosity.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be prepared to not know everything that is going to happen in orientation. 
Go to the social activities. 
Do not sign up for Erasmus Life Budapest, unless you love partying.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you're from the University of Copenhagen it may seem a bit much and challenging that you receive marks on everything you do, but the professors are (in general) very nice and easy-going.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The social experience.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Adapting to the study culture at the university.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
